verdict: Atmos Energy's summer-quarter profit rose 30% to $243M (EPS $1.43) as rate increases and a growing pipeline business lifted operating income 27%.

segments.name: Distribution
segments.note: Delivering natural gas to 3.3 million customers in eight states — the summer quarter is seasonally quiet for heating demand.

segments.name: Pipeline & storage
segments.note: Moving and storing gas, mostly in Texas. Segment revenue was $333M including $229M of sales to Atmos's own distribution arm, which are eliminated in consolidation; shown here on an external basis.

opex.name: Operation & maintenance
opex.note: Crews, pipeline inspections and keeping the network safe — over 85% of capital spending also targets safety and reliability.

opex.name: Depreciation & amortization
opex.note: Spreading the cost of pipes and plants over their lives; it grows as Atmos invests about $4.2B a year.

opex.name: Taxes other than income
opex.note: Property and franchise taxes paid to states and cities.

otherDetail: Interest charges of $33M on utility debt, partly offset by $16M of other non-operating income.

takeaways.title: Net income rose to $243M
takeaways.text: Rate increases already approved by regulators ($355M annualized) flowed through, lifting EPS 23% to $1.43 in the seasonally smallest quarter.

takeaways.title: Pipeline & storage is the growth engine
takeaways.text: Segment revenue rose 22% to $333M (before internal eliminations) on new Texas infrastructure entering service.

takeaways.title: Full-year guidance reaffirmed
takeaways.text: Atmos kept its fiscal 2026 EPS guidance and expects roughly $4.2B of capital spending, recovered through future rates.

footerNote: Purchased gas cost is almost entirely internal in the summer quarter: the pipeline segment sells gas to the distribution segment, and the $229M of internal sales and matching gas cost are eliminated in consolidation, leaving just $8M of net purchased gas cost.
